items.summary_en: EvoGroup selects interaction trajectories using confidence and official task outcomes, then uses the diagnosis to revise tool implementations, retrieval algorithms, prompts, and scheduling policies. The evolved harness is frozen and evaluated on an unseen group-conversation memory benchmark. Its Harness evidence comes from program and policy updates, beyond accumulated memory content; the use of official correctness feedback is not fully unsupervised.

summary_source_claims.paragraph: After the interaction, an official evaluator supplies an external correctness signal y i ∈ { 0 , 1 } y_{i}\in\{0,1\} for the answer a i a_{i} . Combining y i y_{i} with the confidence indicator z i = 𝟏 [ c i > γ ] z_{i}=\mathbf{1}[c_{i}>\gamma] partitions the collected trajectories into four groups:

The Analysis Agent first analyzes evidence within each bucket to identify type-specific issues, and then compares the resulting issues across buckets to derive high-level findings. The resulting condensed rationales and high-level findings F t F_{t} summarize recurring sources of error and brittle success in the current Harness, and provide actionable evidence for subsequent harness revision.

Representation. This interface modifies how information is represented, organized, and linked within the Harness, without changing selection strategies. Updates include restructuring memory units, entity relations, working memory, and the context provided to the underlying model. Operation. This interface adds or modifies executable capabilities and their implementations, such as introducing query tools or revising retrieval algorithms. It determines what the harness can execute and how each operation is implemented. Intervention. This interface introduces checks, transformations, or constraints at execution boundaries, such as validating tool arguments before calls, normalizing returned results, and verifying outputs before returning them as final answers. Policy. This interface modifies the rules governing operation selection, timing, and ordering. Updates include adjusting prompts, skill invocation rules, retrieval parameters, search strategies, and operation composition and scheduling. Based on this distinction, the Evolve Agent selects the interface or interfaces that directly address each diagnosed issue.

Benchmark & Baseline Methods. We use multi-party conversation benchmarks to evaluate the memory capabilities of group-chat agents. EverMemBench ( Hu et al., 2026 ) is divided using stratified sampling, with 30% used as the held-in set for harness evolution and the remaining 70% used as the held-out set for evaluating the evolved harness. To evaluate cross-benchmark transfer, we then freeze the evolved harness and evaluate it on GroupMemBench ( Yang et al., 2026b ) . We compare EvoGroup with structured-memory and self-evolving memory baselines, as well as human-designed agent Harnesses, including (1) FullContext, (2) Mem0 ( Chhikara et al., 2025 ) , (3) MemOS ( Kang et al., 2025 ) , (4) A-MEM ( Xu et al., 2025 ) , (5) MemRL ( Zhang et al., 2026b ) , (6) Codex ( OpenAI, 2025 ) , and (7) Claude Code ( Anthropic, 2025 ) .

items.summary_zh: EvoGroup 根据置信度与官方任务结果选择交互轨迹，再用诊断结果指导修改工具实现、检索算法以及提示和调度策略。演化后的 Harness 冻结后在未见的群聊记忆基准上评估。纳入依据是可执行程序与策略的更新；仅增加群聊记忆内容不构成这些证据，也不能把官方正确性反馈称为完全无监督。

items.summary_en: DualEvolve improves both recommendation solutions and research orchestration. Its outer loop uses process scores and execution traces to add, retire, or merge harness and skill rules that guide later search rounds. The recommendation model is an external research artifact, so the dual-level design alone does not establish coevolution of the agent backbone and harness. The paper also evaluates transfer with frozen rules; reported transfer costs exclude source-rule acquisition.

summary_source_claims.paragraph: Let G G be the number of completed search rounds. At the start of round g ∈ { 0 , … , G − 1 } g\in\{0,\ldots,G-1\} , the state comprises the incumbent mechanism m ( g ) m^{(g)} and orchestration substrate Ω ( g ) \Omega^{(g)} . The substrate contains harness and skill rules governing candidate generation and revision, together with the task-specific inside wiki in Figure 2 . The inside wiki retains candidate records and consolidated lessons from the current task. Orchestration evolution edits the rules; experimental evidence updates the inside wiki. The baseline is m ( 0 ) m^{(0)} , and the final incumbent is m ( G ) m^{(G)} .
DualEvolve alternates mechanism revision under the fixed promotion gate with process-guided updates to the harness and skill rules that shape the next round’s search.

After each round, a menu agent proposes at most one harness edit and one skill edit, each adding, retiring, or merging rules. Thompson sampling chooses among the available edit types and the always-available KEEP action, which applies no menu-proposed edit. The next round’s process reward supplies a delayed utility observation for the selected action type a ( g ) a^{(g)} . With baseline V ( g ) V^{(g)} and 0 < α ≤ 1 0<\alpha\leq 1 ,

After the selected menu action, a separate stagnation check can append direction guidance to the harness, including when that action is KEEP. After one round without promotion, the frozen agent selects a less explored direction from the trial log and records its guidance for the next round when budget remains. Generic mechanism axes provide a deterministic fallback. Menu edits and redirection update the control layer under fixed evaluation and admission. Two consecutive rounds without promotion stop the search. Periodic LLM curation uses runtime evidence to retain useful harness and skill guidance, retire ineffective or contradictory guidance, and merge redundancy.

We initialize Software/NGCF with source-evolved harness and skill rules or the initial rules (No Transfer), holding them fixed for one target round. Runs share the initial mechanism and start with a fresh inside wiki. The transferred rules carry exploration summaries, while raw source logs and wiki entries remain at the source. Each round uses Full’s two-rung schedule and candidate widths 1 ; 3 , 2 , 1 1;3,2,1 . Table 6 reports test performance; source-rule acquisition costs are excluded. Appendix C gives additional transfer and cost details.

items.summary_zh: DualEvolve 在推荐研究中同时改进任务方案和研究编排：外层依据过程评分与执行轨迹增删、合并 Harness 和技能规则，影响后续轮次的搜索。内层改进的推荐模型是外部研究产物，因此不能仅凭“双层”认定 Agent 自身权重与 Harness 共演化。论文另评估冻结规则的迁移，但报告的迁移成本不含源规则获取成本。

items.summary_en: Meta² compares training trajectories and verifier feedback offline to iteratively revise Meta-Skill rules for when and how to intervene. At deployment, these improver rules are frozen and reused to guide harness edits on new tasks. Each online edit affects only its active run and is discarded afterward, without being written back to the Meta-Skill. The inherited artifact is improver decision guidance, rather than a growing collection of global deployment patches.

summary_source_claims.paragraph: Meta 2 answers this question by moving the offline stage one level up. Instead of optimizing a shared harness, it learns reusable evolution Meta-Skill ℳ \mathcal{M} from training trajectories and verifier feedback. At deployment, ℳ \mathcal{M} is frozen, and the evolver decides each within-run edit conditioned on it: δ ( k ) ∼ g ( , ⋅ ∣ h ( k − 1 ) , ℐ ( k ) , ℳ ) \delta^{(k)}\sim g(,\cdot\mid h^{(k-1)},\mathcal{I}^{(k)},\mathcal{M}) . The Meta-Skill is reused across tasks, while each edit affects only its active run. As shown in Figure 2 , Meta 2 has three main components: a checkpoint-based interface for within-run evolution, an offline procedure that learns ℳ \mathcal{M} , and a deployment protocol that reuses ℳ \mathcal{M} without held-out verifier feedback.

Optimize the knowledge, not a single harness. We hold the language model, seed harness, checkpoint interface, and edit channels fixed, and optimize only the evolver’s reusable knowledge ℳ \mathcal{M} . This Meta-Skill links observable execution conditions to three guidance types: act supports an EVOLVE decision, hold supports KEEP, and avoid rules out a specific intervention even when another edit may remain appropriate. The evolver uses this guidance to decide whether and how to edit the harness during a new run. The offline output is therefore reusable decision knowledge rather than a universal harness or a predetermined edit. Offline optimization therefore transfers decision knowledge, not a universal harness or a predetermined edit. Appendix B.1 gives the full offline construction algorithm, and Appendix I specifies the entry fields and content of the Meta-Skill.

A/B/C rollouts make terminal feedback informative. For each training task, we run the same task agent with the same language model and seed harness under three conditions: A , without an evolver; B , with an evolver guided by the current version of ℳ \mathcal{M} ; and C , with an evolver given privileged verifier information available only during training. A–B contrasts compare outcomes with and without the current evolver, whereas B–C contrasts reveal additional recoveries or failures under verifier-informed evolution. Condition C is particularly useful on difficult tasks, where both A and B may fail and their comparison provides no successful examples. By giving the evolver privileged verifier information, C can produce successful rollouts that allow B–C contrasts to reveal recovery strategies missed by the current evolver. To prevent these recoveries from relying on direct verifier leakage, the condition-C evolver’s system prompt strictly prohibits passing privileged verifier information to the task agent. We also audit condition-C trajectories after execution and exclude those that violate this restriction from contrast construction and Meta-Skill learning.

From task-level contrasts to reusable rules. We process training tasks in batches. For batch r r , REFLECT inspects each retained contrastive group and writes candidate entries following the predefined entry schema for each task; AGGREGATE merges recurring patterns across tasks and removes instance-specific details; and UPDATE adds, merges, refines, or deletes entries relative to ℳ ( r − 1 ) \mathcal{M}^{(r-1)} . Let 𝒢 ( r ) \mathcal{G}^{(r)} denote the retained contrastive groups and V ( r ) V^{(r)} their privileged training-time verifier information. The update is

All three stages use LLM calls to the same base model used by the task agent and evolver. After the final batch, the resulting Meta-Skill is frozen for deployment, where it guides edits selected from evidence in each active run.

Freeze globally, adapt locally. At deployment, the learned Meta-Skill ℳ \mathcal{M} is frozen, and every run starts from the same seed harness h ( 0 ) h^{(0)} . At checkpoint k k , the evolver decides an edit conditioned on both ℳ \mathcal{M} and active-run evidence: δ ( k ) ∼ g ( ⋅ ∣ h ( k − 1 ) , ℐ ( k ) , ℳ ) \delta^{(k)}\sim g(\cdot\mid h^{(k-1)},\mathcal{I}^{(k)},\mathcal{M}) . This extends ( 1 ) by explicitly conditioning g g on the reusable knowledge learned offline. The checkpoint interface remains unchanged: KEEP leaves the harness unchanged, while EVOLVE applies δ ( k ) \delta^{(k)} and resumes the task agent with the same environment state and partial trajectory, as described in Section 3.1 . Each edit affects only the remainder of the active run and is discarded when that run ends. Online decisions, task-specific edits, and outcomes are not written back to ℳ \mathcal{M} ; neither held-out verifier feedback nor an LLM-as-a-judge signal is used to update it. The next run therefore reuses the same Meta-Skill and starts again from h ( 0 ) h^{(0)} , carrying over evolution knowledge but none of the preceding run’s harness edits.

A Meta-Skill is a versioned textual library that guides harness evolution at checkpoints. Each entry associates an observable situation with guidance on whether and how to intervene. The evolver interprets these entries using evidence from the active run to select a task-local harness edit or leave the harness unchanged. We denote the frozen library by ℳ = { e i } i = 1 N \mathcal{M}=\{e_{i}\}_{i=1}^{N} , with the entry fields summarized in Table 8 .

items.summary_zh: Meta² 在离线阶段比较训练轨迹与验证反馈，迭代增删 Meta-Skill 中决定何时、如何干预的规则。部署时冻结这套改进器规则，复用于新任务的 Harness 编辑；每次在线编辑只影响当前运行，结束后丢弃，并不写回 Meta-Skill。这里跨任务保留的是改进器决策规则，不能描述成部署时持续积累全局 Harness 补丁。

taxonomy_resolution.reason_zh: 按当前 taxonomy 的功能性分类，Meta-Skill 指导 evolver 决定是否及如何修改 Harness，因此优化对象属于改进器。component 描述其版本化文本库这一工件形式，但没有 improver 精确。学习发生在离线训练批次，部署时 Meta-Skill 固定；不把该分类误说成在线改进器代码持续自改。

items.summary_en: Reglos separates accumulation of user-memory content from improvement of the harness program. An outer coding agent proposes patches to retrieval, ranking, and evidence construction from failure traces, with an independent critic and evaluation selecting retained changes. The qualifying artifact is the program around a frozen task model; the improver and verifier remain fixed. The stricter acceptance rule was adopted after the reported harness was frozen, so it must not be attributed retroactively to all development edits.

summary_source_claims.paragraph: The harness is the program that sits between the memory kernel and the frozen task model and determines what the model reads. It receives the question, together with its answer options where the benchmark provides them, but has no access to the dataset’s labels. Memory is reachable only through a narrow interface: recall, the list of stored items, the user’s profile and the source messages of each fact. Within this interface the harness may issue several recall queries, filter and rank the results across memory layers, and decide how the evidence is organized. These decisions form the search space of the outer loop (Section 3.4 ).

The proposer is the coding agent Claude Code ( Anthropic 2025 ) running Claude Opus 5.5. It reads raw failure traces and writes a patch to the harness, following the finding that raw traces carry more signal than summaries ( Lee et al. 2026b ) . The critic is Codex ( OpenAI 2025 ) running GPT-6.1 Sol, so the proposer and the critic come from different model families. The critic clusters the same failures independently and rejects any patch keyed to the dataset’s option templates or labels. A fixed evaluator then decides. After the freeze, every candidate faces the rule of Figure 4 : it must gain on each of two persona-disjoint validation halves (1,317 questions) and may cost a second reader at most one point; GPT-5.6 Luna is that reader and answers from the same contexts. Humans fix the objective, the splits and the rule; the proposer decides what to change. In the taxonomy of Duan et al. (2026) this is strategy autonomy (L2), and the inner loop is environment adaptation (L4); Appendix C maps both loops onto their components.

Inner loop (per user, in deployment) Outer loop (the harness, offline) Target that user’s record, summaries, profile harness code and prompts: extraction rules, retraction, recall and evidence construction, answer policy Experience the user’s conversations, calendar, corrections failure traces on development splits: context, prediction, gold, recall explanations Improver the fixed write and consolidation pipeline a proposer coding agent (Claude Code) and a critic from a second family (Codex) Strategy fixed rules: add-only extraction, merge adjudication, retraction, Dream cluster failures, form a hypothesis, patch, evaluate Verifier fixed write rules plus user review (inspect, correct, delete, undo) frozen evaluator, pre-registered acceptance rule, second reader Inherited the record itself (append-only history) the accepted harness and the log of candidates and decisions Humans decide what to share, what to correct or delete objective, splits, acceptance rule, when to freeze Level L4, environment adaptation L2, strategy autonomy

In the framework this is strategy autonomy, the level of Self-Harness ( Zhang et al. 2026c ) , and Meta-Harness ( Lee et al. 2026b ) works the same way: the coding agent decides what to change and people decide what counts. The improver and the verifier stay fixed, so the loop stops short of recursive inheritance (L5), where they too would be revised.

During development a change was kept when it did not lower accuracy on the tuning slices, and it replaced the current harness once it gained about 3 points. This margin proved close to run-to-run noise, so after the freeze we adopted the stricter rule of Figure 4 , with GPT-5.6 Luna as the second reader.

items.summary_zh: Reglos 将用户记忆内容的积累与 Harness 程序的改进分开。外层编码 Agent 从失败轨迹提出检索、过滤排序和证据组织的程序补丁，经独立 critic 与评估筛选后保留。纳入的是这套围绕冻结任务模型的程序更新，改进器和验证器本身保持固定。论文在冻结报告版本之后才采用更严格的准入规则，不能称之前的开发改动都通过了该规则。
items.title: Reglos: A Self-Evolving Personal Memory Agent with Recursive Self-Improvement

items.summary_en: HarnessFlow uses MCTS to allocate search across refinement paths of executable harnesses. A coding agent uses a parent design, validation feedback, and execution records to revise context construction, state management, tool use, and stopping rules; candidates and scores persist in the search tree. The harness selected on validation is evaluated on a disjoint test set. Matching candidate-attempt counts does not establish matching total tokens, dollar cost, or compute.

summary_source_claims.paragraph: Given a fixed model m m , task environment, and evaluation protocol, a harness h h is an executable program that governs how the model interacts with tools and the environment. Let ℋ \mathcal{H} denote the space of harnesses compatible with this setting. Refinements may modify mechanisms for context construction, state management, tool use, and termination, as well as their composition and the overall execution structure. For example, adding a verification step may require retaining additional state and revising the stopping rule. The search therefore operates over complete executable harnesses rather than a predefined set of prompts, configurations, or components.

The coding agent develops each candidate from a selected parent harness, guided by accumulated search experience. We denote the experience archive by 𝒜 \mathcal{A} ; it contains prior implementations, code modifications, validation feedback, task-level execution records, and refinement relationships. The parent supplies the starting design, while the archive provides empirical evidence about the effects of earlier changes. The agent can selectively retrieve relevant code and feedback to compare designs, diagnose failures, and identify refinements, without requiring the entire search history to fit in its context.

After n n refinement attempts, the search retains evaluated candidates in a rooted tree 𝒢 n = ( 𝒱 n , ℰ n ) \mathcal{G}_{n}=(\mathcal{V}_{n},\mathcal{E}_{n}) . Each node u i ∈ 𝒱 n u_{i}\in\mathcal{V}_{n} represents a harness h i h_{i} together with its validation score q i q_{i} and execution records ℛ i \mathcal{R}_{i} ; the root u 0 u_{0} represents the initial harness h 0 h_{0} . An edge ( u i , u j ) (u_{i},u_{j}) indicates that h j h_{j} was generated by refining h i h_{i} . Each evaluated harness and its measured score remain unchanged as the tree grows, preserving earlier designs and alternative refinement paths. Expansion counts and accumulated experience evolve with the search. HarnessFlow adapts the MCTS cycle ( Browne et al., 2012 ) through selection, expansion, evaluation, and experience backpropagation.

Evaluating a harness on 𝒟 v \mathcal{D}_{\mathrm{v}} is costly, as each task may require multiple model and tool calls. We therefore consider a sequential optimization protocol initialized from a harness h 0 h_{0} and constrained by a budget of N N refinement attempts. At each attempt, the optimizer draws on accumulated validation scores and execution traces to select an existing harness for refinement and propose a new candidate. The central challenge is to allocate refinement effort across alternative paths while further developing promising designs. At the end of search, we select the harness with the highest observed score on 𝒟 v \mathcal{D}_{\mathrm{v}} among the candidates produced during optimization. The selected harness is then evaluated on a disjoint held-out test set 𝒟 t \mathcal{D}_{\mathrm{t}} , and the resulting score is reported as its final performance.

items.summary_zh: HarnessFlow 用 MCTS 在可执行 Harness 的不同修订路径之间分配搜索。编码 Agent 根据父版本、验证反馈和执行记录提出上下文构造、状态管理、工具使用及终止规则的改动，候选与分数保留在搜索树中供后续迭代。最终按验证集选择的 Harness 再在不相交测试集评估；对齐候选尝试次数不等于对齐全部 token、费用或算力。
items.title: HarnessFlow: MCTS-Guided Harness Optimization for LLM Agents
